newsitem.title: FRANCE: Muscadet vines hit by hailstorms in west France.
newsitem.headline: Muscadet vines hit by hailstorms in west France.

text.p: Freak hailstorms damaged some of the vineyards producing Muscadet wine in western France on Wednesday as storms hammered the north of the country.
Hail bigger than cherrystones fell up to 10 cm (three inches) thick in some areas near the city of Nantes and triggered flooding.

The local chamber of agriculture said some wine producers had complained hailstones had damaged up to 60 percent of their vines, especially near the Grandlieu lake. The region is known for flinty white Muscadet wines, a complement for oysters.
In Paris, a 85-year-old man was crushed to death by a tree felled by high winds in the public park of Les Buttes Chaumont. Another pensioner and a baby were seriously hurt.
